observation.artifact_defect: FREE_SWARM_HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_RECEIPT/v1 captured a per-file size/inode cutoff while its scanner continued to live EOF. Existing-file appends or new workers.jsonl files could therefore enter the Forge DB after cutoff and contaminate global after/delta metrics while cutoff progress still classified the original bytes as caught up. Same-size in-place mutation was not cryptographically bound.
observation.forge_db_defect: before/after metrics were read from the live Forge SQLite using one connection but did not detect commits made by other connections during the receipt, so unrelated concurrent Forge activity could contaminate the bounded evidence window.
observation.counterhypothesis: If the artifact set remains byte-identical and no other SQLite connection commits during the receipt, live scanning/metrics are observationally equivalent to the intended bounded evidence window for these two dimensions. The new guards preserve this positive case.
observation.remaining_limit: The scanner still lacks a true immutable per-file end-mark, so live artifact writers invalidate rather than coexist with a receipt. This is fail-closed but not the final concurrency-friendly design.
